# Insika

> Insika is a Ruby runtime for LLM agents in production: a durable, resumable turn
> pipeline behind an OpenAI-Responses-compatible HTTP API (`POST /v1/responses`), with
> tools, skills, cross-session memory, per-agent policy, content-safety guardrails, and a
> web control UI. Agents are data — created and edited at runtime, no redeploy.

Insika is the operational layer around a model call, not another way to call a model. It
builds on [RubyLLM](https://rubyllm.com) for the chat/tool primitives and adds the parts
production needs: checkpointing, policy, safety, limits, observability and a drop-in API.
Engine overhead is ~0.4 ms p50 per turn.

Every link below is raw markdown — the same files the human-facing site renders at
<https://guizaols.github.io/insika/>. A running instance serves them too, at
`GET /docs/<name>.md` (index at `GET /docs`), alongside its model catalog at
`GET /models.json` and an imperative build-my-first-agent prompt at `GET /start.md`.

## Start here

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/README.md): what Insika is, the one-file first agent, and the router to everything else.
- [Why Insika](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/WHY.md): why a runtime rather than a DIY loop, an assembled framework, or a hosted gateway.
- [Running locally](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/RUNNING-LOCAL.md): boot the engine, the control UI, pointing a Responses client at it, wiring tools to your own backend.
- [Onboarding prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/onboarding/start.md): the skill-structured prompt a coding agent follows to build a first agent (served live at `/start.md`).

## Paste-prompts for your coding agent

One file per journey, same shape as the onboarding prompt — point Claude Code/Codex/Cursor at the URL (a running instance serves each at `GET /docs/<name>.md`) or paste the text:

- [Add a tool or skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/prompts/ADD-TOOL.md): pick data tool vs code tool vs MCP vs skill, wire the allowlist, prove it with one turn.
- [Diagnose a failed turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/prompts/DIAGNOSE-TURN.md): read tasks/events/transcript, map symptom to mechanism, fix one thing.
- [Run every example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/prompts/RUN-EXAMPLES.md): run `examples/` one at a time and explain what each demonstrates.
- [Go live](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/prompts/GO-LIVE.md): mint the two tokens, volume + `WEB_CONCURRENCY=1`, deploy, prove one authenticated turn, close the backup hole.

## Core concepts

- [Agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/AGENTS.md): the AgentProfile and every key on it — creating and editing agents at runtime via the UI, a pack import, or `POST /v1/agents`.
- [Limits and policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/POLICY.md): the five access layers — allowed tools, approvals, content-safety guardrails, edge limits on flood and spend, and reasoning.
- [Tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/TOOLS.md): code tools, data-defined tools, MCP servers, manifests, and egress troubleshooting.
- [Skills](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/SKILLS.md): the SKILL.md format and progressive, on-demand loading.
- [Context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/CONTEXT.md): what fills a turn's prompt, the token budget and eviction, cross-session memory.
- [Workflows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/WORKFLOWS.md): deterministic orchestration of several agents — the five agentic-workflow patterns, schema-validated I/O, durable runs, and when to let the model choose instead.
- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the turn pipeline, the tool-loop, checkpoint recovery, the fiber concurrency model, composition roots.

## Integrate

- [The /v1 API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/API.md): the frozen compatibility contract — the surface, the additive-only rule, the `Insika-Version` gate.
- [Channels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/CHANNELS.md): how people reach the agent: the web widget (one `<script>` tag, no backend of yours, rate-limited because it is public) and the relay (you keep your own WhatsApp/Slack integration and the engine only runs the turn). The engine deliberately does not speak WhatsApp or Slack itself.
- [Media](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/MEDIA.md): photos, voice notes and documents as additive content parts on the message contract; generated images handed back the same way.
- [Embedding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/EMBEDDING.md): mounting Insika into an existing Ruby app — `Insika.embed(backend:)` for a graph that owns its store and credentials, `Insika::Server.rack_app` for the router, and what the process still owns.
- [Plugins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/PLUGINS.md): the two extension tiers — config-only (data tools, MCP, skills) and code (a gem with a manifest that registers tools, policies, middleware or context providers).
- [Templates](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/TEMPLATES.md): the example agents shipped inside the gem — `insika new <name>` or one Studio click gets a running, editable app.

## Ship it

- [Security](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/SECURITY.md): content-safety guardrails, the egress guard, approvals, edge limits, secret handling, and the privacy obligations that come with memory.
- [Sandbox](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/SANDBOX.md): the confined-execution primitive for untrusted tool code.
- [Deploy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/DEPLOY.md): containerized deploy under Falcon, a durable SQLite volume, tokens and environment, and the process model.
- [Router](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/ROUTER.md): `insika-router`, the session-sticky proxy that keeps per-session FIFO, steer and the SSE watch intact across N workers.
- [Releasing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/RELEASING.md): how the gem is cut and how the install is proven from outside the repo before publishing.

## Operate

- [Observability](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/OBSERVABILITY.md): the event stream, plus opt-in OpenTelemetry — turns as traces and metrics, attribute conventions, dashboard recipes.
- [Schedules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/SCHEDULING.md): recurring turns the engine fires on its own tick — one turn per claim window, no catch-up after downtime.
- [Artifacts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/ARTIFACTS.md): a report the agent can hand you a URL to — the `save_artifact` tool, the routes, the expiring signed link.
- [Load test](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/LOADTEST.md): load-testing the engine end-to-end and comparing data topologies.
- [Soak](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/SOAK.md): the long-running stability run and what it is meant to catch.
- [Benchmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/BENCHMARK.md): the neutral, provider-free engine benchmark — methodology, numbers, and how to rerun it without an API key.

## Improve

- [Evals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/EVALS.md): the quality harness — a case as YAML data (deterministic assertions plus a rubric a judge scores), a panel of distinct judge models, and the baseline gate.
- [Refinement](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/REFINEMENT.md): reading an agent's own production traffic back as a ranked failure report — the findings, the window, the privacy rules.
- [Outcomes and follow-ups](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/OUTCOMES.md): the outcome funnel over real traffic and its frozen baseline, plus the follow-up tool that lets an agent come back on a promise it made.
- [Knowledge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/KNOWLEDGE.md): extracting durable concepts from finished conversations into a per-agent knowledge base — the concept format, provenance stamping, PII redaction, and what is not shipped yet.
- [Facts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/FACTS.md): distilling finished customer conversations into proposed facts — human-gated in the Studio, written to memory via CAS, nothing ever applied automatically.
- [Harvest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/HARVEST.md): mining SKILLS from real traffic — the negative list, the evidence-ledger grounding filter, the double gate, snapshot-first promotion, all behind a human approval.

## Reference

- [The domain-free core](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/domain.md): what the gem ships, what a deployment declares, and how to clear the built-in pt-BR corpus.
- [Demo data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guizaols/insika/main/docs/DEMO.md): `insika demo:seed` — one agent populated with a funnel, follow-ups, refinement runs, approvals, facts and evals so a fresh instance shows every loop working.
